Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The two marks sit on the step that manufactures the sine and on the closing reduction; naming the doubling chain stays on the page as unmarked working. NUMERIC CHECK before authoring: the product was evaluated to 12 decimal places as 0.125000000000, which is exactly 1/8. Three cosines give 2³ = 8, and the count of doublings was checked against that. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: See the doubling chain
steps.margin_note: The angles 2π/7, 4π/7, 8π/7 double each time, so this is the standard chain cos θ cos 2θ cos 4θ with θ = 2π/7.

recall.must_convey: That θ = 2π/7 makes the three angles θ, 2θ and 4θ.
accept: put theta as two pi by seven so the others are two theta and four theta
it is cos theta cos two theta cos four theta
theta ni two pi by seven ga teeskuntam

steps.why: The three angles already double, so no rewriting is needed. Naming the smallest angle θ makes the chain visible in one line.
common_mistakes: Trying to work out each cosine as a decimal.
Taking θ as π/7 instead of 2π/7.
steps.memory_tip: Name the smallest angle θ. The other two are then 2θ and 4θ with nothing to change.

steps.label: Multiply and divide by 2³ sin θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Count the cosines: three, so introduce 2³ sin θ. Each 2 pairs with the sine just made and the next cosine, doubling the angle once.
lines: Multiply and divide by 2³ sin θ:
= (1/(8 sin θ)) (2 sin θ cos θ)
[sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, used three times]

recall.must_convey: That 2³ sin θ is introduced top and bottom, and sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ is applied three times to reach sin 8θ.
accept: multiply and divide by eight sin theta so a sine appears
each two pairs with the sine and the next cosine to double the angle
three cosines so three twos and the chain ends at sin eight theta
eight sin theta tho multiply and divide cheyyali
manufacture a sine and use the double angle three times
reject: sin eight theta is sin two pi by seven

steps.why: There is no sine on the left, so one is introduced by multiplying and dividing by the same quantity. Three cosines need three 2s, which is why the denominator is 2³ = 8.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by sin θ without also dividing by it.
Using two 2s instead of three and getting 1/4.
steps.memory_tip: One 2 per cosine. Three cosines means 2³ = 8, and the last angle reached is 8θ.

steps.label: Reduce sin 8θ and finish
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 16π/7 is one full turn of 2π = 14π/7 plus 2π/7, so sin 8θ is sin θ again and the two sines cancel.

recall.must_convey: That sin(16π/7) = sin(2π/7) = sin θ, which cancels the introduced sine and leaves 1/8.
accept: sixteen pi by seven is two pi plus two pi by seven
sin eight theta comes back to sin theta
the sines cancel and one by eight is left
sines cancel ayi one by eight vasthundi
the answer is one by eight
reject: manufacture a sine and use the double angle three times

steps.why: sin(2π + x) = sin x removes the full turn and returns the very sine that was introduced at the start, so it cancels and only the 8 is left.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin θ before reducing sin(16π/7).
steps.memory_tip: 16π/7 is just over one full turn. Take out 2π and the leftover is the starting angle.
